text:
Marathon Petroleum is up modestly today as the stock continues a strong two-week rally—jumping 7.81% since late August. The immediate driver is tightening global refining conditions: diesel prices hit record highs this week after Ukraine damaged Russian refineries and Russia banned diesel exports, while Iran tensions are escalating with new U.S. sanctions and threats of Iranian retaliation. For a refiner like Marathon, this scarcity pushes up the margins they earn on every barrel processed, especially on high-value diesel. U.S. refineries are already running at 98% capacity, leaving little room to ramp up production and capitalizing on these elevated prices.

The broader context amplifies this: the Strait of Hormuz—through which roughly a third of the world's seaborne oil passes—is under fresh geopolitical strain, and a major Venezuelan oil deal announced this week signals a shift in U.S. energy strategy that could reshape global supply dynamics. These structural tightnesses in the market, combined with oil prices holding firm above $91 per barrel domestically, are sustaining the kind of refining environment refiners have benefited from for weeks.
